analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, in documentation and test-procedure prose. It bumps the 'Last updated' date to 2026-11-10 and edits the CI runner-routing description. Cluster GPU shards are now described as routed like the other Mac jobs, no longer as literal Blacksmith runners. The text also adds that a `required` lane keeps its fallback without asking while job sizes are off. Release workflows are still described as pinned to literal Blacksmith runners (head lines ~2056-2061). The patch excerpt is truncated but the range map is complete, and no executable code, workflow, or protocol file is in this batch. The visible head text (lines 1807-2730) contains no secrets or credentials, and its security-relevant statements keep the existing posture. Examples are the release signing lane being dev-only with secrets read only in the signing job, the cache test requiring ephemeral roots and non-persistent keys, and telemetry never carrying tokens or prompts. Threat-model assets touched indirectly are the build and signing pipeline (A-011, A-017) and the cache (T-041). No claimed control is weakened by documentation alone. Open question for integration: whether the underlying workflow change that routes Cluster GPU Tests through the darkbloom plane exists in another file and keeps read-only permissions and fork-PR refusal. The test.md text says scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py pins read-only permissions and fork refusal, but that script and the workflows were not supplied here, so this is an unverified contract, not a finding.
